To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the jet-exit conditions are important to simulate the jet penetration and that a jet issuing into a quiescent flow can be used as a reference to understand how much the presence of the jet affects the jet penetration when the jet is issuing in the crossflow.

the time-average behavior of a transverse jet is influenced by jet-inlet conditions and that the coupling between the crossflow and the jet issuing in the crossflow must be taken into account when the crossflow velocity is high.

1) Jet penetration is affected by the coupling between the issuing jet and the crossflow within the jet pipe; 2) Jet penetration is not affected by the presence of the jet pipe if the jet exit is located sufficiently down the pipe; 3) Simulating the flow in the jet pipe is not necessary for accurate jet penetration predictions if the jet exit velocity is used as the jet inlet velocity; and 4) Jet penetration decreases with the crossflow velocity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of jet-inlet conditions on the time-average behavior of a transverse jet, with specific emphasis in the effect of jet-exit velocity on jet penetration.
the following questions: How far down the pipe does the presence of the wind affect the jet?
the influence of jet-exit conditions on the time-average behavior of a transverse jet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coupling between jet flow and the crossflow is important and should be accounted for when simulating jet penetration.
the coupling between jet exit and crossflow is important and must be taken into account to accurately simulate jet penetration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the jet penetration is affected by the presence of the pipe (nozzle/plenum).

the jet penetration is not significantly affected by the presence of the nozzle/plenum and that the jet penetration can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by neglecting the effect of the crossflow within the plenum/nozzle.

1) the jet-exit conditions are important to simulate the jet behavior and the coupling between jet-exit conditions and the crossflow should not be neglected, and 2) the crossflow velocity at the nozzle exit has to be taken into account in order to reproduce the jet behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper representation of the flow within the nozzle is necessary to obtain an accurate jet penetration.
the jet penetration is strongly dependent on the jet inlet conditions, which must be accurately reproduced in simulations.
a jet issued from a plenum and entering a crossflow should not be modeled by a jet issued from the wall of the crossflow.
